_meta.method: Each state's seven rows were read by hand from where_allowed and local_authority and then checked by script. road comes from roads, bike_lane and separated_bikeway from bike_lanes, bike_path and trail from paths_trails, sidewalk from sidewalks, and footway only where a field names pedestrian paths, otherwise it is unclear. separated_bikeway copies bike_lane, except in Massachusetts where the bikeway sentence sets localMayRestrict. Class 3 limits come from class3_restrictions, and age, helmet, license and speedometer rules are ignored. A class is allowed when the field says it may ride there, says it follows bicycle rules there, or says there is no statewide ban. It is banned when the field says state law bars it. It is unclear when the field is silent, says no rule was found, says the answer is unsettled or hedged, depends on zone, speed or how the bike is classified, or leaves the choice to the managing authority. Where a Class 3 bike is treated as a moped or motor-driven cycle and the fields state no location rule for that category, Class 3 is unclear. localMayRestrict is true when the text says a local authority, state agency or land manager may ban, prohibit or regulate e-bikes or bicycles on that kind, or makes the permission subject to local ordinance. localMayAllow is true only when every banned class in the row can be lifted by a local authority or the managing agency. basis is an exact quote from the named field and supports the most restrictive or least certain value in the row, while the other values come from the field that normally feeds that kind.

trail.basis: Natural-surface non-motorized trails are outside this rule and may be regulated by the agency.

road.basis: Bicycle rules apply (814.405). Where a jurisdiction finds a bike lane or path suitable, riders must use it (814.420).

bike_lane.basis: Allowed, as bicycles. Motorists must yield to e-bike riders in bike lanes (811.050).

separated_bikeway.basis: Allowed, as bicycles. Motorists must yield to e-bike riders in bike lanes (811.050).

bike_path.basis: No e-bike-specific state statute was found. Path and trail rules are set by the managing agency (Oregon State Parks rulemaking in 2024 to 2025, not verified).

sidewalk.basis: BANNED statewide. Riding an e-bike on a sidewalk is 'unsafe operation of a bicycle on a sidewalk', a Class D violation (814.410(1)(e)).

footway.basis: BANNED statewide. Riding an e-bike on a sidewalk is 'unsafe operation of a bicycle on a sidewalk', a Class D violation (814.410(1)(e)).

trail.basis: No e-bike-specific state statute was found. Path and trail rules are set by the managing agency (Oregon State Parks rulemaking in 2024 to 2025, not verified).

road.basis: Class 3 status is unclear (see verdict_cautions). If it counts as a pedalcycle with electric assist, the rules for other e-bikes apply, including the 16 and older age rule. If not, it is most likely a motor-driven cycle (license, registration, insurance).

bike_lane.basis: Class 3 status is unclear (see verdict_cautions). If it counts as a pedalcycle with electric assist, the rules for other e-bikes apply, including the 16 and older age rule. If not, it is most likely a motor-driven cycle (license, registration, insurance).

bike_path.basis: Class 3 status is unclear (see verdict_cautions). If it counts as a pedalcycle with electric assist, the rules for other e-bikes apply, including the 16 and older age rule. If not, it is most likely a motor-driven cycle (license, registration, insurance).

sidewalk.basis: Allowed outside business districts, yielding to pedestrians and signaling before passing. In business districts only where signs permit, and not where a usable bike-only lane is next to the sidewalk (§ 3508).

footway.basis: Allowed outside business districts, yielding to pedestrians and signaling before passing.

trail.basis: Trail access on DCNR and other lands is set by the land manager (not verified).

road.basis: Not addressed in chapter 31-19.7. E-bikes are not motor vehicles. Whether chapter 31-19 bicycle rules apply was not verified.

bike_path.basis: Class 1 is allowed by statute on state bicycle trails and paths. DEM may regulate other uses on its properties (DEM proposed state-park rule amendments in March 2025, not read). Class 2 and 3 access to state paths depends on DEM rules.

sidewalk.basis: Not addressed in the sections read.

footway.basis: Not addressed in the sections read.

trail.basis: Class 1 is allowed by statute on state bicycle trails and paths. DEM may regulate other uses on its properties (DEM proposed state-park rule amendments in March 2025, not read). Class 2 and 3 access to state paths depends on DEM rules.

road.basis: SC has no Class 3 category. A 28 mph Class 3 bike does not meet the § 56-1-10(29) definition (top motor-powered speed must be less than 20 mph).

bike_lane.basis: SC has no Class 3 category. A 28 mph Class 3 bike does not meet the § 56-1-10(29) definition (top motor-powered speed must be less than 20 mph).

separated_bikeway.basis: SC has no Class 3 category. A 28 mph Class 3 bike does not meet the § 56-1-10(29) definition (top motor-powered speed must be less than 20 mph).

bike_path.basis: No statewide e-bike rule found for paths or trails. Land managers and local governments set their own rules.

sidewalk.basis: Whether an e-bike is a 'vehicle' under § 56-1-10(28) (which excludes devices moved by human power) is unclear. Local ordinances apply.

footway.basis: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk rule found.

trail.basis: No statewide e-bike rule found for paths or trails. Land managers and local governments set their own rules.

road.basis: Allowed. Electric bicycles are 'vehicles' (§ 32-14-1(39)) but not 'motor vehicles' (§ 32-14-1(17)), and bicycle rules in Chapter 32-20B apply (ride near the right edge, § 32-20B-5).

bike_lane.basis: No e-bike-specific bike lane rule found. Bicycle rules apply.

separated_bikeway.basis: No e-bike-specific bike lane rule found. Bicycle rules apply.

bike_path.basis: Class III not allowed on a bicycle path or multi-use path unless it is within or adjacent to a highway or roadway, or the managing entity expressly permits it (§ 32-20B-12).

sidewalk.basis: Not confirmed whether 'bicycle' in those sections includes electric bicycles. Municipal ordinances may bar sidewalk riding.

footway.basis: Not confirmed whether 'bicycle' in those sections includes electric bicycles.

trail.basis: Class III allowed on natural-surface nonmotorized trails unless the managing entity prohibits it.

TN.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 55-8-306(a), as amended by 2026 Pub. Ch. 651 § 1

road.basis: Class 1 and 2 allowed anywhere bicycles may travel, but since April 1, 2026 a local government (by ordinance) or a state agency (by rule) may regulate or prohibit Class 1 and 2 on any part of a street or highway where bicycles travel, including state highways, for public safety.

bike_lane.basis: Class 1 and 2 allowed (bike lanes are part of 'any part of a street or highway where bicycles are authorized to travel'), subject to local or state-agency restriction. Class 3 allowed in bike lanes and on shoulders within or next to the street.

separated_bikeway.basis: Class 1 and 2 allowed (bike lanes are part of 'any part of a street or highway where bicycles are authorized to travel'), subject to local or state-agency restriction. Class 3 allowed in bike lanes and on shoulders within or next to the street.

bike_path.basis: Class 3 barred from paths and trails unless the path is within or adjacent to a street or highway or the local government or state agency permits it.

sidewalk.basis: No electric bicycle on a sidewalk unless the local government or state agency authorizes bicycles on that sidewalk AND the electric motor is disabled (§ 55-8-306(a)(4), 2016 text, not changed by Pub. Ch. 651).

footway.basis: No electric bicycle on a sidewalk unless the local government or state agency authorizes bicycles on that sidewalk AND the electric motor is disabled (§ 55-8-306(a)(4), 2016 text, not changed by Pub. Ch. 651).

trail.basis: Class 3 barred from paths and trails unless the path is within or adjacent to a street or highway or the local government or state agency permits it.

road.basis: Allowed. Bicycle rules apply to electric bicycles (§ 551.002). TxDOT and local authorities may not ban e-bikes from highways used mainly by motor vehicles.

bike_lane.basis: Allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed (§ 551.106(a)(2)).

separated_bikeway.basis: Allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed (§ 551.106(a)(2)).

bike_path.basis: All classes allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed, except that TxDOT or a local authority may ban e-bikes on a path that is closed to motor vehicles and has a natural-surface tread made by clearing and grading native soil.

sidewalk.basis: No statewide ban. TxDOT or a local authority may prohibit bicycles (and so e-bikes) on sidewalks (§ 551.106(b)(1)).

footway.basis: No statewide ban. TxDOT or a local authority may prohibit bicycles (and so e-bikes) on sidewalks (§ 551.106(b)(1)).

trail.basis: All classes allowed wherever regular bicycles are allowed, except that TxDOT or a local authority may ban e-bikes on a path that is closed to motor vehicles and has a natural-surface tread made by clearing and grading native soil.

road.basis: Allowed. An electric assisted bicycle follows the bicycle rules in Chapter 6a (§ 41-6a-1115.5(1)).

bike_lane.basis: Allowed. 'Bicycle lane' is defined to include electric assisted bicycle traffic (§ 41-6a-102(8)).

separated_bikeway.basis: Allowed. 'Bicycle lane' is defined to include electric assisted bicycle traffic (§ 41-6a-102(8)).

bike_path.basis: Allowed on paths and trails designated for bicycles, unless a local authority or state agency restricts e-bikes or a class there (§ 41-6a-1115.5(3)).

sidewalk.basis: Bicycle sidewalk rules apply: yield to pedestrians, give an audible signal, ride at a prudent speed. Riders 18+ may not ride where a sign or ordinance prohibits it (§ 41-6a-1106). Local authorities may separately regulate or restrict e-bikes on sidewalks (§ 41-6a-1115.5(3)).

footway.basis: Bicycle sidewalk rules apply: yield to pedestrians, give an audible signal, ride at a prudent speed.

trail.basis: Allowed on paths and trails designated for bicycles, unless a local authority or state agency restricts e-bikes or a class there (§ 41-6a-1115.5(3)).

road.basis: Allowed wherever bicycles are allowed. Banned on Interstate Highway System components except barrier-separated facilities the Commonwealth Transportation Board approves (§ 46.2-908.1).

bike_path.basis: Allowed on bicycle and shared-use paths. After notice and a public hearing, a locality or state agency may ban Class 1 or 2 on a path for public safety or legal compliance. It may ban Class 3 on a path without that process.

sidewalk.basis: Allowed. § 46.2-903 exempts electric power-assisted bicycles from the ban on vehicles on sidewalks.

footway.basis: Allowed. § 46.2-903 exempts electric power-assisted bicycles from the ban on vehicles on sidewalks.

trail.basis: Natural-surface nonmotorized trails may be regulated by the managing body (§ 46.2-904.1(F)(1)-(3)).

road.basis: Allowed. E-bikes are governed as bicycles and riders have bicyclists' rights and duties (§ 1136a(a)).

bike_path.basis: Allowed on bicycle and multiuse paths. After notice and a public hearing, the managing municipality, local authority or State agency may ban Class 1 or 2 on a path for safety or legal reasons. It may ban Class 3 on a path without that process.

sidewalk.basis: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk ban found. § 1132 bars only motor vehicles from sidewalks, and e-bikes are not motor vehicles. Municipal ordinances may regulate.

footway.basis: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk ban found. § 1132 bars only motor vehicles from sidewalks, and e-bikes are not motor vehicles.

trail.basis: On natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized, the path rules do not apply and the managing body may regulate e-bikes (§ 1136a(e)(2)-(4)).

road.basis: Allowed. E-bikes may use highways and park to the same extent as bicycles (RCW 46.61.710(6)). Bicycle rules apply (RCW 46.37.690(3)).

bike_lane.basis: Class 1 and 2 allowed on any part of a highway designated for bicycles. Class 3 allowed on facilities within or adjacent to a highway (RCW 46.61.710(7)-(8)).

separated_bikeway.basis: Class 1 and 2 allowed on any part of a highway designated for bicycles. Class 3 allowed on facilities within or adjacent to a highway (RCW 46.61.710(7)-(8)).

bike_path.basis: Class 3 barred from shared-use paths unless the local jurisdiction allows it.

sidewalk.basis: Class 3 barred from sidewalks unless there is no alternative as part of a bicycle or pedestrian path, or a local ordinance authorizes it (RCW 46.61.710(3), 46.61.715).

footway.basis: Class 3 barred from sidewalks unless there is no alternative as part of a bicycle or pedestrian path, or a local ordinance authorizes it (RCW 46.61.710(3), 46.61.715).

trail.basis: ALL classes barred from natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized unless the managing authority allows them (RCW 46.61.710(9)).

road.basis: Allowed. E-bikes have the same rights and duties as bicycles under chs. 340-351 (§ 346.806(1)), and bicycle provisions of ch. 346 apply to e-bikes (§ 346.02(4)(a)).

bike_path.basis: All classes may ride with the motor on along bikeways (as defined in § 84.60(1)(a)) run by DNR, DOT, a municipality or a county, subject to their rules. A municipality or county may ban powered e-bike use on its bikeways by ordinance, and DNR may do so by rule (§ 349.18(4)).

sidewalk.basis: Not allowed unless local authorities permit it.

footway.basis: Not allowed unless local authorities permit it.

trail.basis: All classes may ride with the motor on along bikeways (as defined in § 84.60(1)(a)) run by DNR, DOT, a municipality or a county, subject to their rules.

road.basis: Allowed. The operator has the rights and duties of the driver of a vehicle under Chapter 17C (§ 17C-11-8(a)). Class 1 and 2 have the same rights as regular bicycles on roads and trails where regular bicycles may go (§ 17C-11-8(h)(1)).

bike_lane.basis: Allowed. Bicyclists must use a marked bicycle lane when riding slower than traffic, with exceptions (§ 17C-11-5(a)).

separated_bikeway.basis: Allowed. Bicyclists must use a marked bicycle lane when riding slower than traffic, with exceptions (§ 17C-11-5(a)).

bike_path.basis: Class 3 barred from bicycle paths, multiuse trails and single-use trails unless within a highway or roadway or the managing municipality, local authority or state agency expressly permits it.

sidewalk.basis: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk rule found. Municipalities regulate bicycle operation under § 17C-2-8(a)(8).

footway.basis: No statewide e-bike or bicycle sidewalk rule found.

trail.basis: Class 3 barred from bicycle paths, multiuse trails and single-use trails unless within a highway or roadway or the managing municipality, local authority or state agency expressly permits it.

road.basis: Allowed with the rights and duties of a vehicle driver (§ 31-5-702).

bike_lane.basis: No e-bike-specific bike lane rule found. Bicycle rules apply.

separated_bikeway.basis: No e-bike-specific bike lane rule found. Bicycle rules apply.

bike_path.basis: No statewide path ban for any class. A local authority or state agency with jurisdiction may regulate any class on trails it manages, including natural-surface nonmotorized trails (§ 31-5-707(f)).

sidewalk.basis: Likely not allowed under motor power. § 31-5-120 bars driving 'any vehicle except motorized wheelchairs other than by human power upon a sidewalk'. Pedaling with the motor off appears allowed. Local ordinances may differ.

footway.basis: Likely not allowed under motor power. § 31-5-120 bars driving 'any vehicle except motorized wheelchairs other than by human power upon a sidewalk'.

trail.basis: No statewide path ban for any class. A local authority or state agency with jurisdiction may regulate any class on trails it manages, including natural-surface nonmotorized trails (§ 31-5-707(f)).
